$description: French copy deck. Extracted VERBATIM from pocket-nutrition-sandbox — the product is French-only and all three clients must show identical wording, so this is the single source a porter copies from rather than retranslating. Keys are stable identifiers; only `fr` and `placeholder` values are translatable.

$extensions.pn.interpolation: Placeholders are {braced}. The sandbox builds these with template literals; a port must substitute the same named values. Where a count drives a plural the rule is stated in `plural` — note it is French (singular at 0 and 1, plural from 2), not English.
$extensions.pn.scope: Every entry carries `scope`: `shared` = reproduce in the native apps AND the sandbox; `sandbox` = specific to the web user-testing prototype and NOT to be ported; `app` = specific to the native apps and NOT present in the sandbox. The welcome screen and the API-gaps panel are researcher/developer surfaces, not product. The journal is the mirror case: the apps persist a local diary, the sandbox persists nothing, so that whole group is `app`.
$extensions.pn.apostropheInconsistency: KNOWN DEFECT, recorded rather than silently fixed. The sandbox mixes the ASCII apostrophe (U+0027) with the typographic apostrophe (U+2019): compare mealBuilder.skipped.one (’) against welcome.step1 ('). French typography wants U+2019 throughout. Values below are verbatim so the inconsistency stays visible; normalising is a copy decision for the design owner, and once taken it should be applied to the sandbox and to this file in the same change.
$extensions.pn.emojiInconsistency: KNOWN DEFECT. The `boiled` method is 🫧 in the method picker (IngredientCard.tsx) and 💧 in the lane header (cookingMeta.ts) — two glyphs for one method on one screen. tokens/cooking-palette.json must record exactly one.

name.context: Header wordmark of the prototype. The apps use the product name instead.

apiLink.context: Header link to the public API.

welcome.$comment: The whole welcome screen is scope=sandbox: it recruits usability-test participants. The native apps have their own onboarding.

intro.fr: Cette application est un prototype conçu pour évaluer la facilité et l'intuitivité du formulaire de saisie d'un repas.

step1.fr: Saisissez le repas que vous avez mangé aujourd'hui, ou un repas typique de votre semaine.

step2.fr: Testez les options — méthode de cuisson, portions, ajout de plusieurs aliments.

step3.fr: Cliquez sur « Analyser » : l'application affichera les valeurs nutritionnelles estimées.

step4.fr: Vous pouvez recommencer autant de fois que vous le souhaitez pour tester différents scénarios.

privacy.fr: Aucune donnée personnelle n'est conservée. Les résultats sont des estimations à titre indicatif.
privacy.context: The apps need their own privacy copy — they DO persist a local diary, so this sentence would be false there.

journal.$comment: The native apps keep a local food diary; the sandbox keeps nothing. There is therefore no sandbox wording to extract for this group — it was written for the apps and belongs to them.

title.context: Home screen title. The app opens here, not on a meal builder.

empty.fr: Aucun repas enregistré pour le moment
empty.context: Empty state, paired with a 🥗 glyph, as mealBuilder.empty is.

add.context: Primary action. Opens the meal builder.

delete.context: Removes one saved meal. Destructive and unconfirmed — an entry is cheap to re-add.

privacy.fr: Vos repas sont enregistrés uniquement sur cet appareil.
privacy.context: Shown on the empty state, where the user is deciding whether to start a diary at all. REQUIRED, not optional: welcome.privacy ("Aucune donnée personnelle n’est conservée") is FALSE for the apps, so shipping that line there would be a false privacy claim.

about.$comment: The about/licences screen. Wholly `app`: the sandbox is a hosted prototype with no store listing, no licence obligation to its visitors and nothing to attribute in-product. Three obligations meet on this one screen — MPL-2.0 §3.2 (a recipient of the executable must be told their rights), the ODbL attribution the Open Food Facts data carries, and the reachable privacy-policy URL both consoles demand before a listing can be submitted. The wording below is a SUMMARY of website.pocketnutrition.org/privacy.html and must not outrun it: if the policy and this screen ever disagree, the app is making a privacy claim nobody reviewed.

title.context: Screen title, reached from the journal.

version.context: {version} is the marketing version — CalVer YYYY.MM.PATCH, e.g. 2026.08.3. Shown because a bug report without it is unactionable.

privacySummary.fr: Votre journal reste sur cet appareil. Aucun compte, aucune publicité, aucun traceur.
privacySummary.context: Condenses the policy's own "En résumé" line. Deliberately makes no claim about the network — privacyNetwork does that, because a summary that stopped here would read as "nothing is ever sent", which is false.

privacyNetwork.fr: Une recherche envoie le texte saisi. Une analyse envoie les aliments, les quantités et les cuissons. Aucun identifiant n’accompagne ces requêtes.
privacyNetwork.context: The two endpoints the app contacts, stated in the app rather than only in the policy. This is the sentence that keeps privacySummary honest.

privacyLink.context: Opens the hosted policy. The same URL the store listings declare.

sourcesBody.fr: Valeurs nutritionnelles : table Ciqual (ANSES). Produits, marques et photos : Open Food Facts, sous licence ODbL.
sourcesBody.context: ATTRIBUTION, not credits. The app displays Open Food Facts labels, brands and product photographs; the Open Database License requires that attribution wherever the database is publicly used. Removing this line would be a licence breach, not a copy edit.

licenceBody.fr: Cette application est un logiciel libre, publié sous licence Mozilla Public License 2.0. Vous pouvez en consulter, en modifier et en redistribuer le code source.
licenceBody.context: MPL-2.0 §3.2 requires that recipients of the executable be informed of these rights. The repository LICENSE file reaches developers; this screen is what reaches the person who installed the app.

sourceLink.context: Opens the public repository. Verified unauthenticated-reachable before shipping — a source link behind a login would make the licenceBody claim untrue in practice.

thirdPartyNone.context: iOS only, and true today: the target links nothing beyond the system frameworks. Android renders a list of components instead — their names and licence identifiers are proper nouns, not translatable copy, so they live in the client.

close.context: Dismisses the screen. Distinct from feedback.close only by group; same word.

empty.fr: Recherchez un aliment ci-dessus pour commencer
empty.context: Empty state, paired with a 🥗 glyph.

analysing.context: Single-character ellipsis U+2026, not three dots.

dropHere.context: Placeholder inside an empty cooking lane.

one.fr: 1 aliment n’a pas pu être ajouté

many.fr: {count} aliments n’ont pas pu être ajoutés

reason.fr: : l’API n’a fourni ni portion de référence (servingG) ni état de consommation exploitable (typicalState, portionMeasuredState). Cette lacune se comble dans Knowledge — le sandbox n’invente aucun poids.
reason.context: Appended to `one`/`many`. The three field names render as inline code. An app must reword the trailing clause — "le sandbox" is the wrong subject there — but must keep the substance, since this is the user-facing expression of the never-invent-food-data rule.

quantity.context: Label beside the grams field on an expanded row.

cooking.context: Label above the cooking-method picker. The sandbox needs no such label: its method is implied by which drop-lane a card sits in, and the apps have no lanes.

remove.context: Removes one row from the meal being composed.

placeholder.fr: Ajouter un ou plusieurs aliments… (riz poulet pomme)
placeholder.context: The parenthetical teaches multi-term search, which is what makes X-Segment-Count meaningful.

showMore.context: Reveals 6 more rows per tap. SANDBOX ONLY, and re-scoped from `shared` when the native clients gained multi-term search: both scroll a capped window instead, because scrolling is the phone's default gesture and a load-more button costs a tap per step. Left at `shared` this would have told a porter to build a control neither app wants.

multiTermHint.fr: Plusieurs aliments d'un coup : « riz poulet pomme »
multiTermHint.context: Sits under the search field and teaches multi-term search, which is otherwise undiscoverable — nothing about a search field suggests that typing three words does anything different. It exists because `placeholder` cannot do this job on a phone: at 51 characters against a field that fits roughly 22, the parenthetical carrying the lesson is exactly what gets truncated. Shown only while the query is a single term; once the server reports a second, the hint has done its work and goes. `app` scope because the sandbox teaches the same thing through its own long placeholder.

alreadyAdded.context: Badge on a suggestion already in the meal.

productBadge.context: Marks an Open Food Facts packaged product rather than a Knowledge ingredient.

sectionRecipes.context: Section header above the recipe rows, which deduplicate-suggestions pins to the top of the list. Before these headers existed the list was flat, and a recipe — the highest-value result, one tap becoming a whole meal — was indistinguishable from an ingredient.

sectionIngredients.context: Section header above curated Knowledge ingredients: productType 'ingredient'. These carry yield factors, serving units and a food group, so they are the results the app can reason about.

sectionProducts.context: Section header above Open Food Facts rows: productType 'off_product'. 'de marque' rather than a bare 'Produits' because the distinction a viewer needs is branded-packaged versus generic food, not product versus non-product. The API reserves these a fifth of the result window.

recipePrefix.context: Recipe row title. Space before the colon — French typography.

recipeComponentCount.context: Not pluralised in the source, so a single-component recipe reads "1 ingrédients". Defect, recorded verbatim.

confirmAdd.context: Multi-select confirm, shown only when more than one search term was typed.

placeholderSingle.context: The short wording the native apps put in the field. NOTE, because the previous version of this note is now wrong: the apps DO have multi-term search — they read X-Segment-Count and offer a multi-select when the query is more than one phrase. They keep this wording anyway because `placeholder` is 51 characters against a field that fits about 22, so the phone would truncate away the "(riz poulet pomme)" that does the teaching. `multiTermHint` carries that under the field instead. Same field, two wordings, for width — no longer because the interaction differs.

drag.context: Accessibility label on the drag handle.

changeCooking.fr: Changer la cuisson et l'état de pesée
changeCooking.context: Accessibility label on the method pill.

report.context: Discreet footer link opening the feedback dialog.

cannotEatRaw.fr: Cet aliment ne se consomme pas cru
cannotEatRaw.context: Tooltip on the disabled "Cru" option when canEatRaw is false.

weighedLabel.context: Non-breaking space before the colon in the source (Pesé :).

weighedInline.context: Inside the method pill; {when} is measuredState.before / .after.

measuredState.$comment: Whether the quantity is a pre- or post-cooking weight. The most consequential control in the UI — see the build-meal-ingredient vector suite.

before.context: Short form inside the method pill.

rawShort.context: Used in "pesé cru" on the results row.

cookingMethods.$comment: Labels and appliance hints per cooking method. Emoji and colours live in tokens/cooking-palette.json under the same method ids. The API also accepts a generic "cooked", which has no picker entry — the client refuses it rather than guessing an appliance.

cookedGeneric.context: Appears only in the feedback form's method list, never as a selectable cooking option.

currentAria.fr: Quantité : {value} {unit}. Toucher pour saisir une valeur exacte.

addUnitAria.context: Increment shortcut from a Knowledge serving unit.

unitMillilitre.context: Capital L, and preceded by a space in rendered weights ("270 mL") unlike grams ("64g"). Pinned by the describe-quantity vector suite.

portionAnchors.$comment: Named portion sizes on the coarse scale. Pinned by the build-anchors and describe-quantity vector suites, so a port must not reword them — the vectors assert these exact strings.

half.context: Shortcut-row multiplier only, not a scale anchor.

onePart.context: Shortcut-row anchor. Capital P, unlike the scale anchor "1 part". Verbatim from the source; both are asserted by vectors.

approx.context: Prefix for an approximate descriptor. U+2248 followed by a space.

portionUnit.context: As in "≈ 1,3 portion" — never pluralised in the source, even above 2.

belowOne.context: Sub-unit weights render this way rather than as "0g".

fiber.context: Hidden when the total is zero.

carbsAbbr.context: Glucides. Note G means carbs here, not grams.

title.context: Live preview above the submit button.

unavailable.context: Shown when available is false. Must NOT be replaced by zeros.

rowSummary.context: Middot U+00B7 with spaces. {method} is the raw API value, untranslated in the source — a defect a port should fix by mapping through cookingMethods.

save.context: Writes the analysed meal to the journal. The sandbox discards its results.

apiGaps.$comment: scope=sandbox throughout: a developer-facing panel documenting known upstream gaps. Do not ship it in a product app.

gap1.fr: typicalState « cooked » n'indique pas la méthode (bouilli, grillé…). Le sandbox ne la devine plus : ces aliments — environ 274 dans Knowledge — sont refusés à l'ajout. Il manque un defaultCookingMethod résolu côté API.

gap2.fr: Portion et état de consommation absents de Knowledge : l'API répond 100 g / cru / pesé cuit par défaut. Ces valeurs viennent du serveur, pas du client — le sandbox n'a plus de table locale.

gap3.fr: Les produits Open Food Facts n'héritent d'aucune métadonnée Knowledge (typical_state, food_group, densité) : source_mappings/off/ est vide, donc ils tombent tous sur les valeurs par défaut ci-dessus.

gap4.fr: densityGMl est renvoyé par l'API mais jamais lu : une quantité en ml est envoyée sans conversion en grammes.

intro.fr: Choisissez une catégorie, puis l'erreur concernée.

referenceWeight.context: Current-value hint shown beside the form.

add.context: Adds one correction to the pending list.

success.fr: Merci, votre signalement a été transmis à l'équipe.

failure.fr: Envoi impossible pour le moment. Réessayez plus tard.

catalog.$comment: The guided-correction taxonomy. CODES ARE NOT COPY: every `code` must match the API allowlist (FeedbackController ALLOWED_CATEGORIES / ALLOWED_CODES) or the submission is rejected. Order is UI order. Only `fr` and `placeholder` are translatable.

errors.placeholder: décrivez le problème ou la nouvelle information

servingUnits.$comment: Mirrors pocket-nutrition-knowledge/serving_unit_types.yaml. A closed vocabulary — do not extend it client-side.

foodGroups.$comment: Mirrors the food_group enum in ingredient.schema.json.

cookingMethods.$comment: Lowercase forms, used in the feedback form only. The picker uses the capitalised forms under the top-level `cookingMethods`.
